title: Why Can You Read While Shaking Your HEAD? 👀
description:
Shake your phone while you read this: blurry. Now hold the phone still and gently shake your head: sharp again. That's your inner ear at work. Its balance sensors feel your head turn and roll your eyes the other way, in about a hundredth of a second (doctors call it the vestibulo-ocular reflex), so the words never slide across the back of your eye. When the phone shakes, your ears feel nothing, so your eyes have to see the movement first and then chase it, roughly ten times slower. In 1948 a young doctor lost this reflex to an antibiotic. He later wrote that he could only read in bed by bracing his head between two metal bars of the bed frame, because even his own pulse made things seem to move. Which one blurred, head or phone?
